title: Therapeutic effects of ginkgetin on rheumatoid arthritis: evidence from network pharmacology and experimental validation.
authors: Zhao, Chengcheng; Yu, Hui; Wang, Jiachen; Xu, Ke; Yang, Mingyi; Xu, Peng
one_liner_zh: 该文研究银杏双黄酮对类风湿关节炎的治疗作用，虽含分子对接但对象为小分子-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disorder characterized by synovial hyperplasia, persistent inflammation, and progressive joint destruction. Ginkgetin (GK), a biflavonoid derived from Ginkgo biloba, exhibits strong anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. However, its therapeutic potential and underlying molecular mechanisms in RA remain insufficiently understood. METHODS: An integrative strategy combining network pharmacology, transcriptomic profiling, molecular docking, and in vitro experiments was applied to elucidate the mechanisms of GK against RA. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified from four GEO datasets of RA synovial tissues, and overlapping targets between GK and RA were screened. Gene Ontology (GO), KEGG pathway enrichment, and protein-protein interaction (PPI) analyses were conducted to identify key pathways and hub genes. Molecular docking and single-cell transcriptomic analyses were performed to predict binding interactions and cellular localization. Finally, MH7A synovial fibroblasts were used to validate GK's effects on inflammation, proliferation, migration, and apoptosis. RESULTS: Thirty-two potential therapeutic targets of GK in RA were identified, among which six hub genes (CXCR4, HIF1A, STAT1, VEGFA, CDK1, and CCNB1) were highlighted. Enrichment analyses indicated that these targets were primarily involved in the HIF-1, VEGF, and cell cycle signaling pathways. Molecular docking demonstrated strong binding affinities between GK and key proteins. In vitro, GK inhibited LPS-induced proliferation and migration of MH7A cells, reduced IL-6 and IL-1beta expression, and promoted apoptosis. qRT-PCR analysis confirmed that GK downregulated all six hub genes, indicating its multi-target regulatory activity on hypoxia, angiogenesis, and inflammatory signaling. CONCLUSION: GK exerts anti-inflammatory, anti-proliferative, and pro-apoptotic effects in RA synovial fibroblasts by modulating multiple signaling pathways, particularly the HIF-1alpha/VEGFA, STAT1, and CXCR4 axes. These findings provide mechanistic insight into GK's pharmacological actions and support its potential as a novel multi-target therapeutic candidate for RA. Key Points *Network pharmacology identified six hub genes (CXCR4, HIF1A, STAT1, VEGFA, CDK1, CCNB1) linking Ginkgetin (GK) to rheumatoid arthritis pathology. *Molecular docking confirmed strong binding affinities of GK with key targets, supporting its multitarget pharmacological potential. *GK inhibits proliferation and migration, suppresses inflammatory cytokines, and promotes apoptosis in LPS-stimulated MH7A synovial fibroblasts. *These findings provide mechanistic evidence supporting GK as a promising multi-target candidate for rheumatoid arthritis therapy.
abstract_zh: 背景：类风湿关节炎（RA）是一种慢性自身免疫性疾病，其特征为滑膜增生、持续性炎症和进行性关节破坏。银杏双黄酮（Ginkgetin, GK）是从银杏中提取的一种双黄酮类化合物，具有显著的抗炎和抗氧化特性。然而，其在RA中的治疗潜力及潜在分子机制尚未得到充分阐明。方法：采用网络药理学、转录组学分析、分子对接和体外实验相结合的综合策略，以阐明GK抗RA的作用机制。从四个RA滑膜组织的GEO数据集中鉴定差异表达基因（DEGs），并筛选GK与RA之间的重叠靶点。进行基因本体论（GO）、KEGG通路富集和蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用（PPI）分析，以识别关键通路和核心基因。通过分子对接和单细胞转录组分析预测结合相互作用和细胞定位。最后，使用MH7A滑膜成纤维细胞验证GK对炎症、增殖、迁移和凋亡的影响。结果：共鉴定出32个GK在RA中的潜在治疗靶点，其中六个核心基因（CXCR4、HIF1A、STAT1、VEGFA、CDK1和CCNB1）被突出显示。富集分析表明，这些靶点主要参与HIF-1、VEGF和细胞周期信号通路。分子对接显示GK与关键蛋白之间具有强结合亲和力。在体外实验中，GK抑制了LPS诱导的MH7A细胞增殖和迁移，降低了IL-6和IL-1β的表达，并促进了凋亡。qRT-PCR分析证实，GK下调了所有六个核心基因，表明其对缺氧、血管生成和炎症信号具有多靶点调控活性。结论：GK通过调节多种信号通路，特别是HIF-1α/VEGFA、STAT1和CXCR4轴，在RA滑膜成纤维细胞中发挥抗炎、抗增殖和促凋亡作用。这些发现为GK的药理作用提供了机制性见解，并支持其作为RA新型多靶点治疗候选药物的潜力。要点 *网络药理学鉴定出六个核心基因（CXCR4、HIF1A、STAT1、VEGFA、CDK1、CCNB1），将银杏双黄酮（GK）与类风湿关节炎病理联系起来。 *分子对接证实GK与关键靶点具有强结合亲和力，支持其多靶点药理潜力。 *GK抑制LPS刺激的MH7A滑膜成纤维细胞的增殖和迁移，抑制炎症细胞因子，并促进凋亡。 *这些发现为GK作为类风湿关节炎治疗的有前景的多靶点候选药物提供了机制性证据。
